title: Vaya Con Dios
mainCopy: GO WITH GOD Stepping out in faith How it started Learn more We are a Christian organization born from the revelation of God’s heart and love for the lost indigenous/ red Indians through one of my dreams. In the dream, I saw two names written in the sky ! David Brainerd and Jonathan Edwards intertwined together. As I woke up, I began to pray and was inspired to do some research online, to see if these Two names ever existed. I found that both were once missionaries called to the indigenous people . David Brainerd Particularly loved and sacrificed his life serving these people but he died under the care of Jonathan Edwards’s daughter at the age of 29 years. He died without raising disciples to carry on the work. Jonathan Edwards was inspired to reach out to the indigenous people after reading the journals that David Brainerd used to keep. Jonathan also died without raising disciples. Having found clarity about who they were and what they did, we began to pray and felt that God was also giving us a burden to reach out to the indigenous people.

title: OUR VISION - Vaya Con Dios
mainCopy: Our vision We are not called to plant churches but to identify aspiring evangelists among the indigenous inorder to raise disciples willing to be trained and equipped and then sent back to evangelize their people. We will also support indigenous pastors who are already in the field with any resources they need to be able to go and preach the gospel. We are also willing to collaborate with the national organisations of the indigenous people as well as the government to come up with a lasting solution to the challenges faced by youth. We are keen to come up with rehabilitation centres that will help and facilitate with these youth to come out of gang or drug related lifestyles. JOIN US

title: What we have done - Vaya Con Dios
mainCopy: What we have done The first pastor we identified was Andreas Jimenez who is married to an indigenous and was sent by his church Iglesia Bautista Prado Centro to Cristiania to work as a missionary in this community. We raised some funds from Christian well wishers and our church and bought him a bike to help him with transport in 2015 First Bike bought 2nd Bike bought Andreas now lives in the community and is working with some youth evangelizing the community. He also has links with Wycliffe Bible School. He has been involved in translating the bible into Embera. The new testament in Embera has now been completed. They are now involved in a discipleship program with the school. The second pastor that we supported is Pastor Fabio Mahecha who was pastoring an indigenous community in San Jose del Guaviare with a bike as well in October 2019. He has since moved and is now pastoring in another village called Inirida Guainia.

title: How it all began - Vaya Con Dios
mainCopy: How it all began Cecilia’s Dream Called to the Indigenous people of the Americas But where? Guatemala?, Minneapolis? – eventually Colombia! Dare we book the flights? Yes! Then the challenges began – opposition Fernando to the rescue Kidnap Finding the reservation Medillin - Colombia Who are the indigenous people? Not just Colombia Displaced and marginalized Customs and beliefs Arrival at Cristiania Social Problems Drug Abuse Alcohol Promiscuity Witchcraft Missing the bare necessities Inadequate Housing Preschool lacks equipment Poverty – single mums, widows and orphans Lack of jobs Poor housing Lack of equipment in school and preschool Lack of land suitable for growing food Malnutrition David and his brother are orphans Mission needs manpower and money but above all prayer Food parcels for single mums Educational equipment Improved housing Tools to deliver the gospel Taking young people on short term mission trips

title: STEPPING OUT IN FAITH - Vaya Con Dios
mainCopy: Stepping out in faith According to the National Indigenous Organization Of Colombia(ONIC) there are 102 indigenous groups in Colombia who live in reservations. When we first made our trip to Colombia in September 2009 we felt led to a village of the Embera Chami called Karamatua (which translates to I am a Christian) also known as Cristiania in the Andes. I initially went with Monica Wisker who also felt the same burden when I shared to go and do what I felt God was calling me to do. We set out not knowing anyone without any contacts armed only with the conviction of the Holy Spirit. How it started God promised to take us there and He has brought us back not only once but every time we have stepped out in faith to respond to his call. He has protected and empowered us, brought people and ministries that have helped us to fulfil this vision. We are eternally grateful to all the people God has used in one way or the other to make this vision a reality. I would like to thank God particularly for Theodora Matowanyika who took over from Monica when she couldn’t travel because of her health etc. We have travelled together as she has faithfully accompanied, supported and encouraged me on this journey to reach the unevangelized. We have seen God move in miraculous ways and we are expecting to experience more of his power and glory .
